# trail: second brain

> A minimalist engine to ingest, connect, and retrieve your organization's collective intelligence. Reimagining Vannevar Bush's 1945 vision with geometric precision.

## Pages

- [Live demo — ask your business — trail: second brain](https://www.trailmem.com/demo/): Ask your business in your own words and get the figures, a chart and the sources — always current, always cited. Illustrative data.
- [Knowledge Infrastructure for the AI Era — Trail reads every source you give it — trail: second brain](https://www.trailmem.com/): Trail reads every source you give it — Word and Excel files, PDFs, pages, notes, conversations — and compiles it into a connected brain of citable Neurons. Ask anything, from anywhere you work, and get the answer with the sources it came from.
- [Onboarding — set up a brain in seven steps — trail: second brain](https://www.trailmem.com/onboarding/): Walk through setting up a Trail brain: name it, pick a template, add sources, invite the team, watch the ingest and ask your first question.
- [Privacy Policy](https://www.trailmem.com/privacy/): What Trail and the Trail Web Clipper do with your data — what the extension reads, what stays on your device, what we store, and how to delete it.
- [The second brain that is everywhere you work](https://www.trailmem.com/second-brain/): Everything you read, hear and save — compiled into one connected memory that remembers for you, and is there wherever you work.
- [Terms of Service](https://www.trailmem.com/terms/): The terms that apply when you use Trail — trailmem.com, the app, the Web Clipper and the embeddable widget.
- [As We May Think: Vannevar Bush's 1945 Vision](https://www.trailmem.com/the-1945-concept/): Explore Vannevar Bush's influential 1945 essay 'As We May Think' and how his vision of information organization shaped modern technology and the internet.
- [Trails — trail: second brain](https://www.trailmem.com/trails/): Essays, field notes, and dispatches from the trail knowledge engine.

## Posts

### dispatches

- [The Orchestration Layer: How broberg.ai Builds Software With Fifteen Agents](https://www.trailmem.com/trails/dispatches/the-orchestration-layer/): Most companies bolted AI onto systems that already existed. broberg.ai built AI-native from the foundation — and then applied the same principle to its own production process. This is what came out: cardmem, an orchestration engine where plans come before code, quality checks happen in a real browser, and the reasoning survives the session.

### how-trail-works

- [Compile-Time Knowledge vs RAG: Technical Architecture Guide](https://www.trailmem.com/trails/how-trail-works/compile-time-knowledge-vs-rag/): Technical analysis of why RAG systems fail for certain workloads. Explore compile-time knowledge architecture as an alternative to retrieval-augmented generation.
- [Does a Trail Get Smarter as It Grows? Knowledge Base Growth](https://www.trailmem.com/trails/how-trail-works/does-a-trail-get-smarter-as-it-grows/): Learn how knowledge bases improve with growth: the S-curve pattern, when systems plateau, and design choices that keep trails smarter.
- [How Brain Memory Works: Trail vs RAG Architecture](https://www.trailmem.com/trails/how-trail-works/how-a-brain-actually-remembers/): Learn how human memory actually works and why Trail compiles knowledge through associative pathways instead of searching like traditional RAG systems.
- [Compile-Time vs Search-Time Knowledge Base Architecture](https://www.trailmem.com/trails/how-trail-works/knowledge-that-compounds/): Learn why compile-time knowledge infrastructure outperforms search-based RAG systems for AI-powered knowledge management and organizational scaling.
- [Trail's Curation Policy: Three Filters on the Gate](https://www.trailmem.com/trails/how-trail-works/three-filters-on-the-gate/): Explore how Trail's three-filter curation policy mirrors the structure of human memory and neural processing for knowledge systems.
- [Trail's Nightly Corpus Processing: Scaling Knowledge Systems](https://www.trailmem.com/trails/how-trail-works/work-that-fits-in-a-night/): Learn how Trail handles the scan wall problem in corpus processing at scale, maintaining full consistency without distributed computing or data loss.

### research

- [Niklas Luhmann's Zettelkasten & the LLM Revolution](https://www.trailmem.com/trails/research/niklas-luhmann-zettelkasten-llm-wiki/): How Luhmann's Zettelkasten method finally became practical with modern AI. Explore the 70-year gap between genius and accessibility.
- [Scaling Trail from 200 to 100,000 Neurons: Engineering Architecture](https://www.trailmem.com/trails/research/scaling-trail-from-200-to-100000-neurons/): Learn how Trail scales from 200 to 100,000 neurons. Explore ingest, lint, and queue workloads, bottlenecks, and architectural solutions for knowledge engines.
- [Three Agent Memory Architectures: Compile vs Retrieve vs Act](https://www.trailmem.com/trails/research/three-architectures-of-agent-memory/): Explore three agent memory architectures—retrieve, compile, and act patterns. Learn why Trail chose the compile pattern and the trade-offs involved.
- [Trail vs NotebookLM: Source-Grounded Knowledge Tools](https://www.trailmem.com/trails/research/trail-and-notebooklm/): Compare Trail and NotebookLM: source-grounded AI tools for knowledge work. Explore their shared ethos and architectural differences.
